(C) is not true since [latex]\left | Z_{1}-Z_{2} \right |\geq \left | Z_{1} \right |-\left | Z_{2} \right |[/latex] (D) is true since [latex] \begin{aligned}\left | Z_{1}+Z_{2} \right |^{2}&=\left ( Z_{1}+Z_{2} \right )\left ( \overline{Z_{1}+Z_{2}} \right ) \\   &=\left ( Z_{1}+Z_{2} \right )\left ( \bar{Z_{1}}+\bar{Z_{2}} \right ) \\   &=Z_{1}\bar{Z_{1}}+Z_{2}\bar{Z_{2}}+Z_{2}\bar{Z_{1}}+Z_{1}\bar{Z_{2}} \;\;...(i)\\ \left | Z_{1}-Z_{2} \right |^{2}&=\left ( Z_{1}+Z_{2} \right )\left ( \overline{Z_{1}-Z_{2}} \right ) \\   &=\left ( Z_{1}-Z_{2} \right )\left ( \bar{Z_{1}}-\bar{Z_{2}} \right ) \\   &=Z_{1}\bar{Z_{1}}+Z_{2}\bar{Z_{2}}-Z_{2}\bar{Z_{1}}-Z_{1}\bar{Z_{2}}\;\;...(ii)\end{aligned}[/latex] Adding (i) and (ii) we get, [latex]\left | Z_{1}+Z_{2} \right |^{2}+\left | Z_{1}-Z_{2} \right |^{2}=2Z_{1}\bar{Z_{2}}+2Z_{2}\bar{Z_{2}} =2\left | Z_{1} \right |^{2}+2\left | Z_{2} \right |^{2}[/latex]

questions.question: The solution of [latex]\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+2\frac{dy}{dx}+17y=0[/latex]; y(0)=1, [latex]\frac{dy}{dx}(\frac{x}{4})=0[/latex] in the range [latex]0 \lt x \lt \frac{\pi}{4}[/latex] is given by
questions.explanation: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+2\frac{dy}{dx}+17y&=0 \\     y\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\    \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}\left ( \frac{\pi }{4} \right )&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex] This is a linear differential equation [latex]\begin{aligned} D^{2}+2D+17&=0 \\   D&=-1\pm 4i \\ \therefore   \;\; y&=C_{1}e^{\left ( -1+4i \right )x}+C_{2}e^{\left ( -1-4i \right )x} \\    &=e^{-x}C_{1}e^{4xi}+C_{2}e^{-4xi} \\    &=e^{-x} \\ \left [ C_{1}\left ( \cos 4x+i\sin 4x \right ) \right ]& +C_{2}\left [ \cos \left ( 4x \right )+i\sin \left ( -4x \right ) \right ]\\ &=e^{-x}\left [ \left ( C_{1}+C_{2} \right )\cos 4x +\left ( C_{1}-C_{2} \right )i\sin 4x \right ] \\ \text{Let } C_{1}+C_{2}&=C_{3} \text{ and }\left ( C_{1}-C_{2} \right )i=C_{4} \\    y&=e^{-x}\left ( C_{3}\cos 4x+C_{4}\sin 4x \right )\\ \text{Since } y\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  1&=e^{-0}\left ( C_{3}\cos 0+C_{4}\sin 0 \right ) \\ \Rightarrow \;\;  C_{3}&=1 \\   \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}&=e^{-x}\left (-4C_{3}\sin 4x+4C_{4}\cos 4x \right ) \\ &-e^{-x}\left [ C_{3}\cos 4x+C_{4}\sin 4x \right ] \\    &=e^{-x}\left [ \left ( -4C_{3}-C_{4} \right )\sin 4x +\left ( 4C_{4}-C_{3}\cos 4x \right ) \right ] \\  \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x} \text{ at } x&=\frac{\pi }{4} \text{ is }0 \\ \therefore \; \left ( -4C_{4}-C_{3} \right )e^{-\pi /4}&=0 \\    4C_{4}&=C_{3} \\    C_{4}&=\frac{C_{3}}{4}=\frac{1}{4} \\ \therefore \;\;    C_{3}&=1 \text{ and }C_{4}=\frac{1}{4} \\    y&=e^{-x}\left ( \cos 4x+\frac{1}{4}\sin 4x \right ) \end{aligned}[/latex]
questions.explanation_html:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}+2\frac{dy}{dx}+17y&=0 \\ y\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}\left ( \frac{\pi }{4} \right )&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
This is a linear differential equation
[latex]\begin{aligned} D^{2}+2D+17&=0 \\ D&=-1\pm 4i \\ \therefore \;\; y&=C_{1}e^{\left ( -1+4i \right )x}+C_{2}e^{\left ( -1-4i \right )x} \\ &=e^{-x}C_{1}e^{4xi}+C_{2}e^{-4xi} \\ &=e^{-x} \\ \left [ C_{1}\left ( \cos 4x+i\sin 4x \right ) \right ]& +C_{2}\left [ \cos \left ( 4x \right )+i\sin \left ( -4x \right ) \right ]\\ &=e^{-x}\left [ \left ( C_{1}+C_{2} \right )\cos 4x +\left ( C_{1}-C_{2} \right )i\sin 4x \right ] \\ \text{Let } C_{1}+C_{2}&=C_{3} \text{ and }\left ( C_{1}-C_{2} \right )i=C_{4} \\ y&=e^{-x}\left ( C_{3}\cos 4x+C_{4}\sin 4x \right )\\ \text{Since } y\left ( 0 \right )&=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 1&=e^{-0}\left ( C_{3}\cos 0+C_{4}\sin 0 \right ) \\ \Rightarrow \;\; C_{3}&=1 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}&=e^{-x}\left (-4C_{3}\sin 4x+4C_{4}\cos 4x \right ) \\ &-e^{-x}\left [ C_{3}\cos 4x+C_{4}\sin 4x \right ] \\ &=e^{-x}\left [ \left ( -4C_{3}-C_{4} \right )\sin 4x +\left ( 4C_{4}-C_{3}\cos 4x \right ) \right ] \\ \frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x} \text{ at } x&=\frac{\pi }{4} \text{ is }0 \\ \therefore \; \left ( -4C_{4}-C_{3} \right )e^{-\pi /4}&=0 \\ 4C_{4}&=C_{3} \\ C_{4}&=\frac{C_{3}}{4}=\frac{1}{4} \\ \therefore \;\; C_{3}&=1 \text{ and }C_{4}=\frac{1}{4} \\ y&=e^{-x}\left ( \cos 4x+\frac{1}{4}\sin 4x \right ) \end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Value of the integral [latex]\oint_{c}(xydy-y^{2}dx)[/latex], where c is the square cut from the first quadrant by the line x=1 and y=1 will be (Use Green's theorem to change the line integral into double integral)
questions.explanation: Green's theorem is, [latex]\begin{aligned} \oint_{c} \phi dx + \Psi dy&=\int_{E}\left ( \frac{\partial \Psi }{\partial x}-\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x} \right )\: dxdy\\ \text{Here }  I&=\oint_{c} \left ( xydy\: -\: y^{2}dx \right ) \\   &=\oint_{c} \left ( -y^{2} \right )dx\: +\: \left ( xy \right )dy \\ \therefore  \;\; \phi &=-y^{2},\; \Psi = xy \\    \frac{\partial \Psi }{\partial x}&=y,\; \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial y}=-2y\end{aligned}[/latex] Substituting in Green's Theorem, we get, [latex] \begin{aligned}  I&= \int_{y=0}^{1}\int_{x=0}^{1}\left [ y-\left ( -2y \right ) \right ]dx\: dy \\   &= \int_{y=0}^{1}\int_{x=0}^{1}\: 3y\: dx\: dy \\   &= \int_{y=0}^{1}\left [ 3xy \right ]_{x=0}^{1}\: dy \\   &= \int_{y=0}^{1}3ydy=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}[/latex]

questions.question: Value of the integral [latex]\oint_{c}(xydy-y^{2}dx)[/latex], where c is the square cut from the first quadrant by the line x=1 and y=1 will be (Use Green's theorem to change the line integral into double integral)
questions.explanation: Green's theorem is, [latex]\begin{aligned} \oint_{c} \phi dx + \Psi dy&=\int_{E}\left ( \frac{\partial \Psi }{\partial x}-\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x} \right )\: dxdy\\ \text{Here }  I&=\oint_{c} \left ( xydy\: -\: y^{2}dx \right ) \\   &=\oint_{c} \left ( -y^{2} \right )dx\: +\: \left ( xy \right )dy \\ \therefore  \;\; \phi &=-y^{2},\; \Psi = xy \\    \frac{\partial \Psi }{\partial x}&=y,\; \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial y}=-2y\end{aligned}[/latex] Substituting in Green's Theorem, we get, [latex] \begin{aligned}  I&= \int_{y=0}^{1}\int_{x=0}^{1}\left [ y-\left ( -2y \right ) \right ]dx\: dy \\   &= \int_{y=0}^{1}\int_{x=0}^{1}\: 3y\: dx\: dy \\   &= \int_{y=0}^{1}\left [ 3xy \right ]_{x=0}^{1}\: dy \\   &= \int_{y=0}^{1}3ydy=\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}[/latex]
